Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Nepal's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. Sana Praveen and Sabitri Dhami will open the innings for Nepal. Australia are starting with spin in the form of Hasrat Gill. A slip in place. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

All eyes will now be on the Nepalese batters, who have faced challenges throughout the tournament, and it won't be any easier against the formidable Australian bowling attack. Can they put up a strong fight and challenge the Aussies? We shall find out soon. Chase coming up shortly...

Caoimhe Bray is in for a chat. She says that it was good to spend time out there. Adds that she was a bit nervous at the start. Shares that there is not much turn on offer. States that they have a good bowling unit and hope to bowl Nepal out. Feels that they have enough runs on the board.

Nepal Women Under-19 impressed with the ball but only in parts. Their catching was excellent though. It was their skipper Puja Mahato leading from the front to claim the opening three wickets. Seemana KC provided able support, picking up two wickets.

Australia Women Under-19 end up with a good total of 139 runs on the board! They endured a turbulent start to their innings, losing three quick wickets to find themselves reeling at 14/3 inside three overs. However, Caoimhe Bray and Eleanor Larosa steadied the ship, forging a crucial 72-run partnership to revive the Australian innings. The partnership was eventually broken when Bray fell for 45 in the 13th over, and Larosa soon followed, departing for 31. Despite this, Australia managed to post a competitive total of 130 runs, thanks in part to a valuable cameo of 30 runs from Hasrat Gill and 16 from Chloe Ainsworth.

Looped up, on a length, on off, Chloe Ainsworth slogs it on the bounce to deep mid-wicket for just a single where Jyotsnika Marasini mops it up. 15 runs off the final over. Australia Women Under-19 end with 139 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-match formalities now. Nepal Women Under-19 fielders spread out and take their respective fielding positions. Kate Pelle and Ines McKeon walk in with their blades for Australia Women Under-19. Puja Mahato has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
We are all set to begin. The two teams stride out in the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Nepal's first, followed by the national anthem of Australia.

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainford is pitchside. He feels that this is a good batting wicket but spinners could get some turn. Feels that sweeping against the spinners will be a good option. Reckons that bowlers will have to be consistent with their lines and lengths to contain the scoring.

The captain of Nepal Women Under-19, Puja Mahato says that they were looking to bowl first. Adds that in a T20 game, anything can happen and they learnt a lot from the previous game. Ends by informing that Tirsana Bishwokarma comes in for Kiran Kunwar.

The captain of Australia Women Under-19, Lucy Hamilton says that this looks like a hard wicket and this is a good opportunity to put a big total on the board. Mentions that in the previous two games, they bowled first and this is an opportunity to show their batting strength. Informs that Lily Bassingthwaighte comes in for Tegan Williamson.

Nepal Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Sana Praveen, Sabitri Dhami, Puja Mahato (C), Jyotsnika Marasini, Seemana KC, Alisha Yadav (WK), Tirsana Bishwokarma (In for Kiran Kunwar), Krishma Gurung, Anu Kadayat, Rachana Chaudhary, Riya Sharma.

Australia Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Kate Pelle, Ines McKeon, Lucy Hamilton (C), Caoimhe Bray, Eleanor Larosa, Hasrat Gill, Ella Briscoe, Grace Lyons (WK), Chloe Ainsworth, Lily Bassingthwaighte (In for Tegan Williamson), Juliette Morton.
TOSS - Australia Women Under-19 win the toss and they will BAT first.

Nepal Women Under-19, despite losing both their games, have shown promise in their bowling department and will be seeking to spring a surprise and cause a major upset. Their recent match against Scotland Women Under-19 was a close one, with Seemana KC and Rachana Chaudhary picking up two wickets each. Can Nepal build on this performance and pull off a stunning victory, or will Australia's dominance continue? We shall find out together. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

The stage is set for an exciting clash in Match 20 of the ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup 2025, as Australia Women Under-19 take on Nepal Women Under-19. A tournament favorite, Australia boasts a strong and well-rounded squad with a potent batting lineup and a formidable bowling attack. Led by talented players Ines McKeon and skipper Lucy Hamilton, Australia will look to assert their dominance and secure a comprehensive victory. Australia's impressive form has seen them convincingly defeat Scotland Women Under-19 by 9 wickets, chasing down the total inside 7 overs. In their second match, they controlled the game against Bangladesh Women Under-19, limiting them to 91 runs despite strong resistance. Although Australia experienced a dramatic collapse, Ella Briscoe's calmness guided them to victory with two wickets remaining. Nepal Women Under-19, on the other hand, are seeking to spring a surprise and cause a major upset. Despite losing both their games, Nepal's bowling department has shown promise, and they will need to be at the top of their game to contain the Australian batters. Nepal's recent match against Scotland Women Under-19 went down to the wire, with Scotland winning by just one wicket. Seemana KC and Rachana Chaudhary picked up two wickets each for Nepal, and they will look to build on this performance against Australia.
